h: Yaakov’s Covenant Unites the Opposites and Makes Israel Endure

p: אַתֶּם נִצָּבִים הַיּוֹם כּוּלְּכֶם (דְּבָרִים כט, ט)
"You are standing today, all of you" (Devarim 29:9).
Atem has the letters of emes,
and this is the seal of Hashem Yisbarach.
why it opened in the plural, "you," etc.,
"for you to pass into the covenant."
And in Rashi, of blessed memory:
What is the meaning of this?
וּבְמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (תַּנְחוּמָא נִצָּבִים ג)
And in Midrash Tanchuma on this parshah (Tanchuma, Nitzavim 3):
"Like a person who says to his fellow,
if you go back on me
Now regarding the covenant in this parshah,
it is stated in the holy Zohar
that ten levels are counted here,
and they correspond to the Ten Commandments;
And in Midrash Tanchuma on this parshah (ibid.):
וְלָמָּה כָּרַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עִמָּהֶן כָּאן
"and why did HaKadosh Baruch Hu make one with them here?
Because the one at Sinai they nullified."
Seemingly, what is this expression, "they nullified it"?
Why, it is written in the Torah forever,
and a single letter of the Torah
will never, chas v'shalom, be nullified,
עַל יוּ״ד שֶׁבְּיַרְבֶּה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ו, א)
about the yud of yarbeh (Shemos Rabbah 6:1):
but a thorn of you I will not nullify."
He should have said "they transgressed it."
indicates that Hashem Yisbarach agreed to this;
and how can one say such a thing,
שֶׁחַס וְשָׁלוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִסְכִּים לָזֶה
that, chas v'shalom, Hashem Yisbarach agreed to this?
"These are the words of the covenant";
And in Midrash Tanchuma (on this parshah)
"The wicked are overturned and are no more,
but the house of the righteous will stand."
"The wicked are overturned and are no more":
this is the generation of the Flood, and Sedom, and more;
and "the house of the righteous" refers to Yisrael.
But what is the meaning of "the house,"
and what is the endurance meant by "will stand"?
as is known, came from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
And this is why the parshah
אִם בְּחֻקּוֹתַי תֵּלֵכוּ וְגוֹמֵר (וַיִּקְרָא כו, ג)
"If you walk in My statutes," etc. (Vayikra 26:3);
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה יט, א)
as they said in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah 19:1):
meaning that one aims at the will of Hashem Yisbarach
And this is why it brings there,
and turned my feet to Your testimonies":
to the shuls and the batei midrash";
that is, by themselves, without his awareness.
וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this is the aspect of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
who was an unblemished olah offering
and did not deviate from the will of Hashem Yisbarach
And this is from the side of Gevurah;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג פ, ב)
and of this it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 80b):
"The Torah emerges from the side of Gevurah."
אֲבָל מִי יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת מְבוֹרָר כָּל כָּךְ
But who can be so clarified
כִּי מִי יֹאמַר זִכִּיתִי לִבִּי (מִשְׁלֵי כ, ט)
For "who can say, I have purified my heart?" (Mishlei 20:9).
the one in the previous parshah,
which is the book of teshuvah;
that is, if the Jew does teshuvah,
אָז אַף שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מְכַוֵּין כָּל כָּךְ
then even though he did not aim so fully
at the depth of the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
Hashem Yisbarach conducts Himself with him in mercy.
And these Moshe said on his own,
(as is written at the end of Megillah, Megillah 31b),
for he was lenient with them;
וְלָזֶה לֹא כָּתַב כָּאן רַק מִצְוֹתַי
and therefore here it wrote only "My commandments,"
that is, all the six hundred thirteen mitzvos
וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this is the aspect of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
and kept My charge, My commandments," etc.
Although "My statutes" is also written there,
הַיְינוּ אִם מְקַיֵּים רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
that is, if he fulfills the will of Hashem Yisbarach
in the mitzvos as they are written,
to aim also at the statutes,
at the depth of the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
even without awareness, as mentioned above.
And the third covenant, the one in this parshah,
הוּא כְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him;
do not yet have complete perfection,
that the redemption from Egypt corresponds to vav-hei,
זֶה הָיָה מִצַּד בְּחִינַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
this was from the aspect of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
and it does not yet have perfection,
for there were still claims there:
רַק הָיָה בְּמִדַּת הַחֶסֶד לְפִי שָׁעָה
it was only through the middah of Chesed for the moment.
וְכֵן מִצַּד יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And likewise from the side of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
there is also not yet perfection,
כִּי אֵין הָעוֹלָם יָכוֹל לְהִתְקַיֵּים בְּמִדָּה זוֹ
for the world cannot endure through this middah,
as Chazal, of blessed memory, said:
to create the world with the attribute of Justice;
He saw that the world would not endure,
so He joined with it the attribute of Mercy."
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים פח, א)
And this is what Chazal said (Pesachim 88a):
"Not like Avraham, who called it a mountain,"
from all the matters of this world,
and then Hashem Yisbarach appeared to him,
"As it is said to this day,
on the mountain of Hashem," etc.;
"and not like Yitzchak, who called it a field,"
which is the field of apples;
that is, as soon as he sensed
he would give himself over to Hashem,
and he was called an unblemished olah.
there is not yet complete perfection;
for each middah on its own,
only in its place is it good.
And therefore from them there still came forth dross,
"The wicked are overturned and are no more";
that is, when Hashem Yisbarach conducts the world
with the middah that pertains to him,
But the covenant in this parshah
הוּא כְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
who holds on to both sides;
and this is Yaakov, who called it a house.
And this is "but the house of the righteous will stand":
for this is called a house,
and from him no more dross came forth.

Yaakov Joins Both Sides in One House

p: And this is why He brought into this covenant
even though in truth they are two opposites.
that is, one who conducts himself with the middah of wisdom,
for wisdom is in the head,
וְאֵיזֶה חָכָם הָרוֹאֶה אֶת הַנּוֹלָד (תָּמִיד לב, א)
and "who is wise? One who sees what will come about" (Tamid 32a).
Opposite it is "your little ones" in the second five,
that is, one who knows only the present.
that is, one who rules over himself,
"The scepter shall not depart from Yehudah,"
"One who exercises rule shall not pass away," etc.;
that is, he has firmness within himself,
to be the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
who do not have a settled mind,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תּוֹסָפוֹת רֵישׁ חוּלִּין)
as Chazal said (Tosafos at the beginning of Chullin, 2a):
and she easily lets herself be persuaded.
that is, one who gives counsel to his soul,
so that even the body will be drawn
to the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
that is, even though he has drawn himself
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צד, א)
"These are those who rule with a rod";
that is, even though words of Torah
אֵינָם מִתְקַבְּלִים תֵּיכֶף עַל לֵב הָאָדָם
are not immediately accepted by a person's heart,
"And now, if you will surely listen to My voice,"
and Rashi, of blessed memory, explained:
"If now you accept it upon yourselves,
it will be pleasant for you from here on,
And opposite this is "from your woodchopper,"
that is, one who wants immediately
to see the receiving of reward,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּאָבוֹת (אָבוֹת ד, ה)
along the lines of what Chazal said in Avos (Avos 4:5):
"and not a spade to dig with."
and it alludes to the one
who aims at the depth of the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
And opposite him is "up to your water-drawer,"
that is, one who is immersed
to all the cravings and desires,
עִם כׇּל זֶה הִכְנִיס כּוּלָּם בַּבְּרִית
Nonetheless He brought them all into the covenant;
that is, one who is always drawn
after the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
then even if it sometimes happens
that he is on a low level,
the will of Hashem Yisbarach that he be on this level.
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין רוֹאֶה אֶת הַנּוֹלָד כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
that is, one who does not see what will come about, as mentioned above:
at the time of Matan Torah
that they put "we will do" before "we will hear,"
and were not concerned at all
that perhaps they would be unable to fulfill it,
that this Sadducee said to Rava:
that is, one who does not stand firm in her view
and they expounded in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Korach 10)
"The wisest of women builds her house."
שֶׁאֵין הַגּוּף נִמְשָׁךְ עוֹד כָּל כָּךְ
whose body is not yet drawn so much
after the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
Seemingly, why does it not say
"and the convert who is in the camp,"
and what is the expression "your convert"?
that in every one of Yisrael there is
a point that is called a "convert,"
which comes from a foreign place,
"From your woodchopper up to your water-drawer,"
that is, those who are still immersed
in the desires of this world:
לִפְעָמִים בָּא מִזֶּה גַּם כֵּן טוֹב
sometimes good also comes from this,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים סח, ב)
"At first, when a person acts, it is for himself
that is, since a person is in a body,
to aim immediately for the sake of Heaven;
rather, out of doing it not for its own sake
he will come to do it for its own sake.
And therefore this too is good,
and this is from the side of the level of Yaakov.
And from where did he merit this?
עַל זֶה אָמַר לְעָבְרְךָ בִּבְרִית וְגוֹמֵר
Of this it says, "for you to pass into the covenant," etc.,
and Rashi explained, "that you should be passing";
brings himself into a curse and an oath;
even though if he does not fulfill it
he will be punished for it,
מְקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ הָעוֹנֶשׁ גַּם כֵּן
he also accepts the punishment upon himself
so that even if he is on a low level,
גַּם אָז הָיָה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּזֶה
then too it was the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
וְזֶה הָיָה מַדְרֵגַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this was the level of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him:
after he received the blessings from his father,
that this was not by chance,
in that Rivkah sensed it beforehand,
וְעֵשָׂו לֹא בָּא עַד שֶׁהוּא יָצָא
and Esav did not come until he had left,
been firm in his mind from this
that Hashem Yisbarach certainly agreed to it,
and he should have been resolute;
Rather, he went to Lavan, to a place of impurity,
and left and parted from such a father.
וְכׇל זֶה הָיָה לְבָרֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ
And all this was to clarify himself;
הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִסְכִּים עִמּוֹ
that is, although Hashem Yisbarach agreed with him,
that Hashem Yisbarach does not give for nothing,
And therefore he went into exile
Although Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
הָיָה לוֹ מַאֲמַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל זֶה
he had a statement of Hashem Yisbarach about it,
such as "Go forth" and the like.
brought himself, on his own, into trials.
And this is the meaning of "that you should be passing,"
as it says in the Midrash cited above:
"Like a person who says to his fellow,
that even if he is on a low level,
Hashem Yisbarach will agree with him
that at this time this is good.
And this is the aspect of truth,
the middah of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
And this is what it says in this covenant:

Accepting the Covenant Through Personal Resolve
